rocks.name: ORDINARY BASALT
rocks.clue: Interesting rock! But we need stronger evidence of past water. Weak evidence does not mean there was NO water.

rocks.name: HEMATITE SPHERES
rocks.clue: These tiny hematite spheres can be clues to ancient water. Opportunity found many of them, nicknamed "blueberries".

rocks.name: DUSTY SOIL
rocks.clue: Windblown dust and soil. Wind shapes Mars too: this patch tells us little about ancient water.
rocks.result: Windblown dust: no water clue here.

rocks.name: GYPSUM VEIN
rocks.clue: A bright vein in the rock. Veins like this likely formed when water flowed through underground cracks, leaving calcium minerals behind.
rocks.result: Forms when water moves through cracks.

rocks.name: CLAY-RICH ROCK
rocks.clue: Clay minerals! Opportunity found clays that formed in neutral-pH water: the friendliest conditions it studied.
rocks.result: Clays form in water that is not very acidic.

rocks.name: JAROSITE OUTCROP
rocks.clue: Layered outcrop with jarosite, a mineral that forms in acidic water.
